Dorian did not look at the world; he looked at the wireframe beneath it. Standing before the Living Atlas, he adjusted the focal length of the crystalline projector. The holographic projection mapped thousands of crustal sensors in real-time, detailing the intricate relativistic magnetohydrodynamic shear between the Red Giant's infrared coronal mass ejections and the Blue Dwarf's compressed ultraviolet bow shock. It was a chaotic storm of opposing forces, painting the bruised violet twilight outside with double razor-sharp shadows across the hand-built brass observatory roof. He was looking at the shear vectors, isolating the exact threshold where the magnetosphere would buckle. 

"The telemetry is undeniable," Dorian murmured to himself, the glow of the projection illuminating his sharp features. The entire Enclave stood in the shadow of two suns, and the deep subterranean bioluminescent wonder they had cultivated was now pulsing in a frantic, irregular rhythm. "We need to defend against the thermal spike," he concluded, analyzing the sensory data cascading down the optical quartz array. His mind whirred, processing the variables through his precise, unyielding logic. He could see the structural stress points, taste the ozone tang in the air, smell the scorched ozone creeping through the vents, and hear the low hum of the generators working overtime. The heat radiating from the brass fittings was palpable. Then, the realization hit him. The conductivity of the entire base was elevated.

He strode into the kitchen, the heart of the Hub. "Leo," Dorian called out, spotting the artificer across the room. "The magnetic shear is driving auroral ionization down to bedrock. The entire Forge is conductive." He pointed a long, ink-stained finger at the dining table. "I need you to ground every metal soup spoon in the kitchen. Immediately." 

Silas paused, a ladle hovering over a massive pot of stew, raising an eyebrow at the absurdity of the command. "If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong," Dorian added dryly, catching Silas's expression. The tension in the room thickened as the storm battered against the reinforced walls. Suddenly, a massive atmospheric discharge rattled the entire structure. Dorian's measured caution evaporated in the face of the overwhelming data. The sheer audacity of the phenomenon demanded a response. "Then today is a good day for science," he declared, his voice ringing out over the storm, handing the grounding wire to Jane and preparing to consume the stew despite the imminent danger.
